items.author: Nikunj Kothari
items.summary: FPV Ventures partner Nikunj Kothari scraped the sub-processor lists of 803 AI-native companies to see what infrastructure they really use. 44% now list two or more model providers (up from 33% in March), and Anthropic grew twice as fast as OpenAI, though on a small sample. 33% list an inference provider (up from 22%), Modal keeps winning there, and Chinese models show up mainly through video (Bytedance) rather than text. He cautions that sub-processor lists lag reality; the data is at deploygraph dot com.
items.summaryZh: FPV Ventures 合伙人 Nikunj Kothari 爬取了 803 家 AI 原生公司的 sub-processor 名单,想看看它们实际用了哪些基础设施。列出两家及以上模型提供商的公司占 44%(3 月为 33%),其中 Anthropic 的增速是 OpenAI 的两倍,不过样本量不大。列出推理服务商的占 33%(此前为 22%),Modal 依然领跑,而中国模型主要通过视频(如 Bytedance)而非文本进入。他也提醒,sub-processor 名单是滞后指标;完整数据在 deploygraph dot com。

items.author: Aditya Agarwal
items.role: General Partner at SPC; co-founder of Bevel Health; ex-CTO of Dropbox
items.summary: SPC general partner Aditya Agarwal says there are only two kinds of companies worth building now. The first is diffusion of AI: vertical SaaS-style businesses that put AI right where the work happens, like Profound, Cognition and Harvey. The second, and his bet for where most model-driven returns will come from, is the frontier: using AI to speed up science, then building products from the results, such as Externa (protein chemistry), Epana Bio (autoimmune therapies), VenomicsAI and Equivariant (semiconductor modeling).
items.summaryZh: SPC 普通合伙人 Aditya Agarwal 认为,现在值得做的公司只有两类。第一类是 AI 的扩散:类似今天 vertical SaaS 的模式,把 AI 送到工作发生的地方,例如 Profound、Cognition 和 Harvey。第二类是 AI 的前沿,也是他认为绝大部分模型驱动回报的来源:用 AI 加速科学进步,再基于成果做产品,例如 Externa(蛋白质化学)、Epana Bio(自身免疫疗法)、VenomicsAI 和 Equivariant(半导体建模)。

items.author: Amjad Masad
items.summary: Replit CEO Amjad Masad finds the timing of the Jensen Huang stories suspicious: why do old, barely hidden stories suddenly become international news? His speculation is that if Huang, the leading champion of open models, is removed, anyone who wants AI closed and centralized benefits, and he points to the midterms and upcoming IPOs as possible reasons for the timing. It is an opinion and a question, not a claim of evidence.
items.summaryZh: Replit CEO Amjad Masad 觉得 Jensen Huang 相关报道的时间点很可疑:为什么那些本来就没怎么被掩盖的旧事,突然成了国际和地缘政治新闻?他的推测是,如果最有力的开源模型倡导者 Huang 被拿下,所有希望 AI 封闭、集中、受控的人都会受益,而中期选举和即将到来的 IPO 可能是选在此时的原因。这是一种观点和提问,并非有证据的断言。

items.author: Garry Tan
items.role: President and CEO of Y Combinator
items.summary: Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan calls it ill-advised for Nvidia's board to oust Jensen Huang, given how central Huang's leadership is to the company's operations. He argues Huang's day-to-day work is "prime actor work" and that a transition would be hard to imagine without a massive market-cap implosion.
items.summaryZh: Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan 认为,Nvidia 董事会罢免 Jensen Huang 是不明智的,因为 Huang 的领导力对公司运营至关重要。他说 Huang 的日常工作属于"prime actor work"(主角才能做的事),很难想象交接不会带来市值的大幅蒸发。

items.author: Dan Shipper
items.summary: Every CEO Dan Shipper argues that benchmark curves like GDPval (AI beating human experts 12.4% of the time in 2024, about 83% in 2026) miss why teams still matter. In one experiment, Claude given 400 attempts reproduced his Slack answers 93% of the time, but when asked to rank its own answers, his landed in its top 10% only about 60% of the time. Generating possibilities is cheap; knowing which matter is the human part, so he wants AI measured on doing your work from your perspective.
items.summaryZh: Every CEO Dan Shipper 指出,像 GDPval 这样的基准曲线(AI 击败人类专家的比例从 2024 年的 12.4% 升到 2026 年约 83%)忽略了团队依然重要的原因。在一项实验中,Claude 给出 400 次尝试时,93% 的情况下能复现他在 Slack 里的回答;但让它给自己的答案排序时,他的真实答案只有约 60% 的概率排进前 10%。生成可能性很便宜,判断哪些重要才是人的价值,所以他主张用"从我的视角完成我的工作"来衡量 AI。

items.author: AI & I by Every
items.title: A New Vision for Human Work After Automation
items.takeaway: When everyone has the same frontier model, the default answer becomes the baseline, and the value lies in the perspective and responsibility you bring to push past it.
items.takeawayZh: 当所有人都能用同一个前沿模型时,默认答案就成了基准线,真正的价值在于你带着自己的视角和责任把它推得更远。
items.summary:
Every CEO Dan Shipper closed the company's first conference with a way to think about the future of work. There are two ways to predict it: the aggregate, extrapolating a trend line from lots of data, and the intimate, zooming into one real case. The aggregate says AI now beats experts about 83% of the time on GDPval. The intimate view is his own week: in the cracks of his calendar he analyzed a customer survey, built a game for the team, vibe coded a CRM and sent cold emails, work he prices at five people and roughly $200K in 2020 terms.

But when his whole team got the same survey and the same Claude, each found something different. His go-to-market engineer saw first-time subscribers churning over too much email, the marketing head saw readers who feel lonely in their AI enthusiasm, and an editor built a Claymation game show. A default prompt gives the answer anyone could get. In an internal test, Claude could produce what Shipper would say in Slack 93% of the time given 400 tries, but could only rank it in its top 10% about 60% of the time. "Generation is really cheap, but ranking is hard."

The rebuttal that models will learn to rank misses that people improve too: compare 2027 Yash with 2027 Claude against the default prompt, and the model cancels out. His conclusion is to measure AI by "how good is it at doing my work from my perspective," not just on problems everyone agrees are worth solving.
items.summaryZh:
Every CEO Dan Shipper 在公司首届大会的压轴演讲中,提出了一种看待未来工作的方式。预测未来有两种方法:aggregate(大量数据外推趋势线)和 intimate(放大观察一个真实案例)。aggregate 的结论是,AI 在 GDPval 上约 83% 的时间能击败专家。而 intimate 的视角就是他自己的一周:在日程的缝隙里,他分析了客户调查、给团队做了游戏、vibe coding 了一个 CRM 并发出开发邮件,按 2020 年的标准相当于五个人、约 20 万美元的工作量。

但当整个团队拿到同样的调查数据和同样的 Claude 时,每个人发现的东西都不一样。负责 go-to-market 的工程师发现新订阅者因为邮件太多而流失,市场负责人发现读者对 AI 的热情让他们在身边显得很孤独,一位编辑则做了一档黏土动画问答节目。默认 prompt 只会给出人人都能得到的答案。在一项内部测试中,给 Claude 400 次尝试,它有 93% 的概率生成出 Shipper 会在 Slack 里说的话,但让它排序时,真实答案只有约 60% 的概率排进前 10%。"生成很便宜,排序很难。"

"模型迟早会学会排序"这个反驳忽略了人也在进步:拿 2027 年的 Yash 加上 2027 年的 Claude,对比默认 prompt,模型这一项就抵消了。他的结论是,衡量 AI 不应只看人人公认值得解决的问题,而应看"它从我的视角做我的工作有多好"。
